mission.title: openyurt: Add Claude Code Skills for deploying OpenYurt and configuring Raven
mission.description: Deploying OpenYurt and configuring Raven today requires a long sequence of manual Helm and kubectl steps spread across docs, and openyurtio/openyurt#2559 reports that "Add Claude Code Skills for deploying OpenYurt and configuring Raven" is needed so an AI assistant can drive the deployment. This mission adds a Claude Code skill (`.claude/skills/deploy-openyurt/`) to the repository: a short SKILL.md entrypoint plus reference docs covering the Helm install and Raven gateway setup.

steps.title: Scaffold the skill directory in the openyurt repository
steps.description:
Create the Claude Code skill layout proposed in the issue — a short entrypoint file with detailed reference docs beside it:
```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills/deploy-openyurt/references
touch .claude/skills/deploy-openyurt/SKILL.md
touch .claude/skills/deploy-openyurt/references/helm-install.md
touch .claude/skills/deploy-openyurt/references/raven-config.md
```
The skill format (one `SKILL.md` per directory) is used instead of flat `.claude/commands/` files so the entrypoint stays short while the reference docs hold the detail.

steps.title: Write the SKILL.md entrypoint with scoped frontmatter
steps.description:
Define the skill with frontmatter that scopes `allowed-tools` to only what the deployment needs (read-only kubectl plus helm), keeping the AI from running arbitrary commands:
```markdown
---
name: deploy-openyurt
description: Deploy OpenYurt via Helm and configure Raven cross-network communication
allowed-tools: Bash(helm:*), Bash(kubectl:*), Read, Grep
---

Deploy OpenYurt into the current cluster, then configure Raven.
Follow references/helm-install.md for the Helm steps and
references/raven-config.md for the Raven gateway setup.
Verify each phase before moving to the next.
```

steps.title: Add the Helm deployment reference for yurt-manager and raven-agent
steps.description:
Fill `references/helm-install.md` with the exact chart commands the skill should execute:
```bash
helm repo add openyurt https://openyurtio.github.io/openyurt-helm
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install yurt-manager openyurt/yurt-manager -n kube-system
helm upgrade --install raven-agent openyurt/raven-agent -n kube-system
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l 'app.kubernetes.io/name in (yurt-manager,raven-agent)'
```
Keeping these commands in one reference file means a chart parameter change only requires editing this file, not hunting through a monolithic command file.

steps.title: Add the Raven gateway configuration reference
steps.description:
Fill `references/raven-config.md` with the Gateway custom resource and the node labelling Raven needs to route cross-network traffic between cloud and edge node pools:
```bash
kubectl label node <gateway-node> raven.openyurt.io/gateway=gw-cloud
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: raven.openyurt.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: gw-cloud
spec:
  exposeType: PublicIP
  endpoints:
    - nodeName: <gateway-node>
      underNAT: false
YAML
kubectl get gateways.raven.openyurt.io gw-cloud -o yaml
```

steps.title: Validate the skill end-to-end with Claude Code
steps.description:
From the repository root, invoke the skill and confirm it drives a working deployment:
```bash
claude "/deploy-openyurt"
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=yurt-manager
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=raven-agent
kubectl get gateways.raven.openyurt.io
```
All pods should be Running and the Gateway should list an active endpoint; if the skill stalls, check that `allowed-tools` in SKILL.md covers every command the reference docs use.

resolution.summary: The repository had no agent-readable deployment instructions, so AI assistants could not reliably deploy OpenYurt or configure Raven — the knowledge lived only in scattered human docs. Adding a Claude Code skill fixes this because the short SKILL.md entrypoint gives the assistant a stable contract while the reference docs hold the operational detail: a Helm chart parameter change only requires editing one reference file, not hunting through a monolithic command file. Scoping `allowed-tools` in the frontmatter works as the safety boundary because Claude Code refuses any tool invocation outside that list, limiting the skill to helm/kubectl operations.
